FAST

Nov 25 : AI-linked stocks extended their slide in premarket trading on Wednesday, with chipmakers, server makers and data center operators all falling as investors weighed the soaring cost of the AI infrastructure buildout against its returns.
Investors have set a high bar for AI-linked companies, punishing shortfalls and offering little reward for beating expectations and raising outlooks, as concerns grow over heavy, often debt-fueled infrastructure spending and uncertain returns.
Dell Technologies slumped 7.2 per cent on Wednesday despite the server maker raising its annual revenue and profit forecasts for the third time this year and approving an additional $25 billion share buyback.
"Investors are focused on the big and rising cost of building AI, so good earnings and impressive earnings forecasts no longer lift sentiment," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote Bank.

Rival AI server maker HPE tumbled 16.3 per cent on Tuesday after raising its full-year revenue outlook. Its shares and those of rival Super Micro declined 5.2 per cent and 3.6 per cent, respectively, on Wednesday.
Shares of Ambarella, valued at $2 billion, tumbled 36 per cent after the AI semiconductor firm forecast fourth-quarter revenue below analysts' estimates.
Nvidia, which has been at the heart of the turmoil, fell 4.6 per cent, extending Tuesday's 6 per cent slide, as the rally sparked by CEO Jensen Huang's rehiring quickly lost steam.
Anthropic dropped 5.6 per cent, trading well below its $83 initial public offering price just days after the Claude developer's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.
DEBT STRAIN
Neocloud providers, which rent out specialized AI computing capacity, have been under pressure since October over concerns about the debt funding their rapid expansion.
The Democrats' victory in the midterm elections this month has added to those worries, with investors weighing the prospect of a data center slowdown from tougher AI regulation and more hurdles to construction.
Nvidia-backed neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius Group each fell about 6 per cent, while IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific lost more than 4 per cent.
The yield on CoreWeave's bonds due 2031 rose to almost 18 per cent as prices fell more than 1.6 cents on the dollar to near record lows, Tradeweb data showed.
The cost of insurance against tech companies defaulting on debts has jumped sharply, with five-year CDS spreads at Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave hitting record levels.
Shares of AI hyperscalers were broadly lower, with Oracle, Alphabet, Amazon.com, Meta Platforms and Microsoft down between 1.4 per cent and 4.3 per cent.

Source: Reuters

FAST

NEW DELHI, Nov 25 : After India failed to bowl out New Zealand on a placid Basin Reserve pitch in Wellington on Monday, their captain Shubman Gill made a passionate plea for the return of legal ball management in test cricket.
With the 2018 ball-tampering scandal involving Australia in South Africa firmly back in the spotlight after recent developments players, coaches, umpires and TV cameramen are keeping a sharp eye out for potential infractions.
Ball tampering has declined in the glare of that spotlight with the result that reverse swing bowling has become more difficult.
Ball management became even harder in 2020, when COVID-19 gripped the world and the ICC banned the use of saliva for health reasons, and Gill thinks the ban has long served its purpose and should be lifted.

"There was a rule that you can't put saliva on the ball to make it shine," he told reporters. 
"It's been seven to eight years and I still don't understand why they are not allowing it. If you're not able to maintain the ball, especially on wickets like these, it makes the job of the bowlers very difficult."
The ICC has no plans to lift the saliva ban, however, because it considers the practice unhygienic.
The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), responsible for the laws of the game, has not budged from its support for the ban and offered no new comment when contacted by Reuters.
Its 2022 statement said the ban had "little or no impact" on swing and removed "grey areas around fielders eating sugary sweets to alter their saliva".
REVERSE SWING GREATS
Fielders and bowlers may still use sweat to shine the ball, but it is less effective.
The craft was developed by Pakistan fast bowlers Wasim Akram and Waqar Younis, who wreaked havoc with an old ball by using its polished side to bend deliveries wickedly late in flight.
Batters could no longer relax after seeing off the new ball, because the old one brought different challenges, swerving late and in the opposite direction to conventional swing.
The skill demands meticulous ball management - shining one side and scuffing up the other to exploit aerodynamics.
The sight of fielders rubbing saliva on the ball and red streaks on bowlers' white clothing were evidence of legal means to shine the ball, and scuffing could be achieved by bowling or throwing it against rough grass.
There were, however, more furtive methods.
In 2000, Waqar became the first player suspended for ball-tampering. India great Sachin Tendulkar and former England captain Mike Atherton were accused of similar breaches while South Africa's Faf du Plessis was sanctioned twice, once for applying saliva from a mint to shine the ball.
The ICC's harshest punishments for the offences were fines and suspended match bans.
That changed in 2018, when TV cameras caught Australia's Cameron Bancroft with a piece of sandpaper in his hands during the third test against South Africa at Newlands.
Bancroft, then captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner took responsibility for a plot to scuff up one side of the ball. Smith received a one-match ban and a fine from the ICC, Bancroft a fine, and Warner no punishment.
GREY AREA
The Australian public, however, recoiled in horror at its players being caught in the act of cheating and Cricket Australia quickly responded with severe punishments previously handed out only for match-fixing. 
The ICC later upgraded ball-tampering to a level-three offence with stiffer penalties and cases dropped considerably.
Former Australia batter and coach Justin Langer recently argued that "Sandpapergate" had all but killed the craft by frightening players away from preparing the ball.
Scuffing remains a perennial grey area.
Throwing the ball into the dirt or across an abrasive outfield, or rolling it in the wicketkeeper's gloves, does not sufficiently roughen the surface, and anything beyond that amounts to ball-tampering.
The ICC men's cricket committee supports reverse swing, provided it stays clear of ball-tampering. It has also explored a return to a single new ball in one-day internationals, rather than two used from opposite ends, so the ball ages and can be made to reverse swing.
Former England batter Dawid Malan would give practitioners some leeway.
"Historically, over the game, people have been caught trying to tamper with the ball for years," he said on a BBC podcast this year.
"It's not a new thing. I actually think you should legalise it, like just let people scratch the ball.
"Obviously, do not bring things in from outside. But it's a skill in itself — to be able to get the ball to reverse swing. It will make cricket a lot more bowler-friendly."

Source: Reuters

FAST

LONDON, Nov 25 : New Zealand centre Jordie Barrett has rejected assertions of All Blacks fatigue, but both they and South Africa are struggling at the end of an intensive year which included a four-test series between the two top-ranked teams.
South Africa will play in Sunday’s Nations Championship final despite successive defeats by France and Ireland, while the All Blacks are reeling from a shock loss to Wales and a record drubbing by England.
They face England again on Saturday in the tournament’s third and fourth place playoff, their 17th international this year.
"They are just inconvenient facts. We are not going to use any excuse language this week," Barrett told reporters.

"We need to be better. We have been off the mark in the past few weeks and we have been a little bit inconsistent all season, but we are going to throw everything we can at it this week," he added.
Barrett's defiant approach, however, runs against considered opinion with former All Blacks coach Graham Henry saying the team had hit a wall and ex-flyhalf Tony Brown believes the series against the Springboks in August and September caused a fatigue factor.
Brown is now a coach with the Springboks but will join the All Blacks coaching team after next year’s World Cup.
"Coming off the Greatest Rivalry tour, which was probably the most intense four test matches either country has played probably ever, and trying to perform well in a northern hemisphere tour, is hard," Brown said.
"If you lose a little bit of your momentum or mojo on attack, then your game suffers. I think the All Blacks are in a similar spot to us and not quite at their best, like we’re not.
"But luckily for us we get a chance against France in the final this weekend and I know the All Blacks will perform well against England in their last game of the year. I don’t have any concerns over whether the All Blacks will beat England."

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

English regulator won't shy away from action against Man City, says Kogan

LONDON, Nov 25 : English football's new independent regulator will not shy away from taking action against Manchester City, chair David Kogan said on Wednesday, insisting the body must prove it is willing to act regardless of a club's size.
An independent commission in September found City guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. The club are appealing the verdict and have denied any wrongdoing.
Speaking before parliament's Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee, Kogan said the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) would be obliged to fulfil its statutory duties if triggered by the outcome of the case against City.
"We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," Kogan told MPs.

"We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action that's laid out in the legislation depending on the circumstances as they come to us."
Kogan said the regulator would not be deterred by the prospect of taking on one of the country's biggest clubs.
"Would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early? Well, probably not," he said. "But the truth is, if we don't act, assuming those circumstances are triggered, what is the purpose of a local regulator?
"I think we have to absolutely clearly be seen to be doing the job that you as legislators have asked us to do. And we absolutely will do it, whatever that means."
Under the Football Governance Act 2025, the regulator could impose licence conditions on Manchester City or remove or disqualify owners and directors found not to have acted with honesty and integrity, and even force a sale.
Kogan said any future action would be driven solely by evidence and the requirements of legislation.
"The politics around this issue are not my concern," he said. "The issue that I have to deal with, that Richard (Monks, the IFR's CEO) has to deal with, and our staff have to deal with, is does the evidence, if we come to assess it in relation to individuals, stand up in terms of the legislation as being the cause for concern?
"If it is, we will have to act appropriately. And that is the only test. Not the politics around it, not the place where it came from, not the size of the club."
Kogan said the regulator's credibility depended on demonstrating it was prepared to tackle difficult cases.
"You cannot have an effective regulator without applying the rules consistently," he added. "We haven't spent all this time and energy as a group getting this together to undermine it at the first big test."

Source: Reuters

items.title: María Lorena Gutiérrez se va de Grupo Aval tras dos años en la Presidencia
items.author: Daniel Guerrero
items.summary: La ejecutiva presentó su renuncia ante la Junta Directiva del conglomerado financiero, al que estuvo vinculada durante cerca de ocho años. En una carta a los empleados hizo un balance de su gestión.
items.body: Bogotá — María Lorena Gutiérrez presentó su renuncia a la Presidencia de Grupo Aval, uno de los mayores conglomerados financieros de Colombia, tras dos años y medio al frente de la organización y cerca de ocho años de trayectoria dentro del grupo empresarial. “He tomado la decisión de cerrar esta etapa profesional y presenté mi renuncia ante la Junta Directiva”, aseguró la ejecutiva en una carta dirigida a los colaboradores de la organización, fechada este 25 de noviembre de 2026. Gutiérrez, quien ha ocupado cargos de alto nivel tanto en el sector público como en el privado, destacó entre los resultados de su administración la recuperación de la rentabilidad del grupo, la integración de negocios fiduciarios y la incursión en el ecosistema de pagos. “A lo largo de mi carrera, estudiando y trabajando con organizaciones y líderes muy distintos, he aprendido que parte del liderazgo es saber cuándo poner fin a una responsabilidad”, expresó. En su carta de despedida, la ejecutiva destacó que en 2025 y 2026 el grupo alcanzó una utilidad neta superior en 70% frente a 2024 y que en el segundo trimestre de este año registró su mayor rentabilidad sobre el patrimonio en cuatro años. También resaltó la consolidación de la integración de los negocios fiduciarios en Aval Fiduciaria y la entrada al ecosistema de pagos con GoU Payments. “Ampliando nuestra participación en la cadena de valor de los servicios financieros y desarrollando nuevas capacidades de negocio”, señaló al referirse a esta última operación. Durante su administración, el conglomerado también avanzó en la centralización de procesos de abastecimiento, ciberseguridad, nómina y reclutamiento, como parte de su estrategia de captura de sinergias a través de Aval Valor Compartido. En materia de sostenibilidad, Gutiérrez destacó que la organización se ubicó entre el 5% de las mejores del mundo por sus prácticas e impacto ambiental, social y económico. La ejecutiva también deja definida la estrategia corporativa para el período 2026-2031, que contempla objetivos de crecimiento, desarrollo de negocios, eficiencias operativas, gestión de riesgos y transformación tecnológica. María Lorena Gutiérrez asumió la Presidencia de Grupo Aval el primero de abril de 2024, convirtiéndose en la primera mujer en ocupar ese cargo y sucediendo a Luis Carlos Sarmiento Gutiérrez. Su nombramiento representó un cambio en la dirección del conglomerado financiero, cuyo liderazgo había estado históricamente en manos de la familia Sarmiento. Antes de llegar a la cabeza del holding financiero, Gutiérrez se desempeñó durante cerca de seis años como presidenta de Corficolombiana, compañía de inversiones con presencia en sectores como infraestructura, energía, gas, hotelería y agroindustria. Llegó a esa organización en agosto de 2018, después de finalizar su paso por el Gobierno de Juan Manuel Santos. La carrera profesional de Gutiérrez ha transcurrido entre la academia, el Gobierno y el sector empresarial. Es ingeniera industrial de la Universidad de los Andes, institución en la que también cursó estudios de posgrado en Finanzas. Cuenta con una maestría en Administración de Empresas (MBA) y un doctorado en Finanzas de la Universidad de Tulane, en Estados Unidos. En la academia se desempeñó como decana de la Facultad de Administración de la Universidad de los Andes, antes de ocupar altas responsabilidades en el Gobierno colombiano. Entre 2010 y 2016 hizo parte del equipo de la Presidencia de la República durante la administración de Juan Manuel Santos. Posteriormente, fue embajadora de Colombia en Alemania entre 2016 y 2017. Regresó al Gobierno nacional como ministra de Comercio, Industria y Turismo, cargo que ejerció entre 2017 y 2018, antes de dar el salto a Corficolombiana. En la carta dirigida a los colaboradores del conglomerado financiero, Gutiérrez no precisó la fecha en la que se hará efectiva su renuncia ni reveló quién la sucederá en el cargo. El relevo se producirá en la organización que reúne a entidades como Banco de Bogotá, Banco de Occidente, Banco Popular, Banco AV Villas, Corficolombiana y la administradora de fondos de pensiones y cesantías Porvenir. En su mensaje de despedida, Gutiérrez atribuyó los resultados alcanzados durante su administración al trabajo colectivo de los empleados del conglomerado. “Cada logro lo compartimos entre todos, porque siempre he creído que ese es el verdadero sentido de un equipo: asumir juntos los retos, reconocer el aporte de cada uno, y entender que los resultados nunca son mérito de una sola persona”.

items.title: Macklem says inflation forecast is lower, but oil price pressures are lingering
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem says falling global oil prices could mean inflation ends the year below the central bank’s last forecast.
items.body: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem says falling global oil prices could mean inflation ends the year below the central bank’s last forecast. The Bank of Canada said back in October that it saw inflation rising to 3.5 per cent by the end of the year as stubbornly high global oil prices threatened to put more pressure on consumers. Statistics Canada said inflation held steady at 3.1 per cent in October. High gas prices from war in the Middle East continued to be the biggest driver of inflation, but the agency said upward pressure was broad-based across groceries and clothing as well. Macklem suggested at a press conference in Toronto on Tuesday that recent relief at the gas pumps should mean inflation holds around those levels through the end of the year. “The inflation forecast is a bit lower. Those costs that built up over the previous eight months, they’re still there, but there’s a bit of edge (that’s) come off the inflation forecast,” he said. The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by a quarter point to 2.5 per cent in October as it warned gas prices were staying higher for longer than first expected and inflationary pressures could start to spread. Officials signalled at the time that they’d “proceed carefully,” but there could be a need for more rate hikes to come. Macklem also addressed the current inflation outlook in a speech to the Economic Club of Canada in Toronto on Tuesday. While he acknowledged the recent climbdown in global benchmark oil prices, he said that wasn’t the only factor monetary policymakers were weighing. “So far, businesses have largely absorbed the higher production and transport costs. But historical lags and our own business surveys suggest more pass-through to consumer prices in the year ahead. This second-round effect of the oil shock will add to inflation persistence,” he said in prepared remarks. CIBC chief economist Avery Shenfeld said in a note to clients on Tuesday that the governor seemed to be downplaying the disinflationary impact of falling oil prices. Shenfeld said Macklem’s focus on lingering inflation risks suggests the central bank could be gearing up to deliver a second consecutive rate hike at its next decision on Dec. 9. “There was no direct reference to the December meeting, but what was apparent was that the governor was going out of his way to not show any changes in his thinking from October whenever possible,” he said. Odds of a quarter-point hike from the Bank of Canada next month stood at 79 per cent as of Tuesday, according to LSEG Data & Analytics. That’s up from nearly 63 per cent on Monday. Macklem said Tuesday the Bank of Canada will be weighing next week’s releases of gross domestic product data for the third quarter and November labour market figures before deciding what to do at its final policy rate decision of the year. --- Craig Lord, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 24, 2026.

items.title: Global stocks are mixed as AI shares tumble after a retreat on Wall Street
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: World stocks were mixed on Wednesday after a wave of heavy selling of stocks linked to artificial intelligence once again hit Wall Street.
items.body: HONG KONG — World stocks were mixed on Wednesday after a wave of heavy selling of stocks linked to artificial intelligence once again hit Wall Street. U.S. futures slipped and oil prices also fell. Relief over Nvidia’s decision to restore Jensen Huang as its CEO has been tempered by questions over the chipmaker’s corporate governance and President Donald Trump’s influence. In early European trading, Germany’s DAX was up 0.1 per cent to 25,046.66. In Paris, the CAC 40 rose 1 per cent to 8,120.72, while Britain’s FTSE 100 gained 0.5 per cent to 10,515.74. The future for the S&P 500 was 0.8 per cent lower, while the future for the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.3 per cent. In Asian trading, Taiwan’s Taiex tumbled 5 per cent as AI chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. sank 3.6 per cent. Chip designer Mediatek plunged 10 per cent. In South Korea, the Kospi lost 6.2 per cent to 4,697.51 as Samsung Electronics fell 9.9 per cent. SK Hynix plummeted 11.1 per cent. Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8 per cent to 57,011.62. Shares of OpenAI investor SoftBank Group slumped 14.8 per cent and semiconductor maker Kioxia plunged 14.2 per cent. The Hang Seng in Hong Kong slipped 1.1 per cent to 21,966.01. The Shanghai Composite index declined 2 per cent to 3,476.47, falling to its lowest level in more than a year. The Trump administration is expected to soon announce plans to raise tariffs on China and 15 other trading partners. China recorded a record trade surplus of nearly US$1.2 trillion last year. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged 0.4 per cent lower to 8,692.40. The consumer price index in October rose to 4.9 per cent from a year earlier, topping expectations. That could put pressure on the central bank to raise interest rates. India’s Sensex rose 1.5 per cent. On Tuesday, stocks tied to the artificial intelligence industry dragged the U.S. market lower after a surge the day before quickly fizzled. That’s even though much of the rest of Wall Street rose, along with confidence among Americans in the economy. The S&P 500 fell 0.5 per cent to its eighth loss in the last nine days. The Nasdaq composite shed 1.5 per cent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.9 per cent. They’re the latest swings for a market that’s been mostly sinking since hitting its all-time high last month. The surprise return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO, announced Monday, does bring back a charismatic leader who championed the entire AI industry. But it does not settle deeper concerns such as whether AI can possibly produce enough profit and productivity to justify massive investments in data centers. High interest rates are making it more difficult to borrow money to pay for the industry’s growth. Sweeping victories for Democrats earlier this month in the U.S. midterm elections, meanwhile, have raised the possibility of more regulation for AI, potentially slowing construction of data centers. Nvidia fell 5.9 per cent a day after soaring 31.5 per cent to its biggest gain in more than two decades. Other stocks around the AI industry fell by similar amounts. And Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, sank 6.5 per cent to drop below $83. That’s how much Anthropic first sold its stock for in its initial public offering last week. The stock had briefly jumped as high as $115 in its first day of trading amid a frenzy of hype. Such drops were powerful enough to drag the S&P 500 index lower even though most of the stocks within the index climbed. They rose following the latest report to say confidence among U.S. consumers is improving by more than economists expected. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil, the international standard, climbed 2.4 per cent to $88.78. It’s been yo-yoing between $72 and $114 since the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February. Early Wednesday, Brent was down 1.5 per cent to $87.43 a barrel. U.S. benchmark crude oil dropped 1.8 per cent to $80.56 per barrel. The U.S. dollar rose to 159.42 Japanese yen from 159.26 yen. The euro slid to US$1.0944 from $1.0966. Elaine Lai, The Associated Press

LONDON, Nov 25 : Former England winger Raheem Sterling was spared an immediate jail sentence on Wednesday after he admitted dangerous driving by inhaling 'laughing gas' while behind the wheel before crashing his Lamborghini.
Sterling, who won four Premier League titles with Manchester City and made 82 appearances for England, was sentenced to 12 months' imprisonment, suspended for 18 months, and ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work.
The 31-year-old appeared in the dock at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court where Judge Kirsty Allman said he had acted with "conscious disregard for the safety of other road users". Sterling was also disqualified from driving for two years.

Sterling was reported driving erratically on the M25 and M3 motorways in southern England during the morning rush hour on May 28, with dashcam footage showing him weaving between lanes and almost colliding with the central reservation on the M3.
One witness who called the police said Sterling's driving was "absolutely horrendous", saying he had been inhaling from a large balloon which covered most of his view of the road.
After leaving the motorway, Sterling's Lamborghini struck a sign at the side of the road causing extensive damage to his vehicle, which Judge Allman said was no longer capable of being driven. No other vehicle was involved and no one was hurt.
Police found Sterling sitting in the passenger seat of his crashed car holding two canisters of nitrous oxide. He later told police that he had a "problem with nitrous oxide".
Sterling, who played for Dutch club Feyenoord last season, pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide and failing to provide a blood specimen.
His lawyer Jason Bartfeld said Sterling had started consuming nitrous oxide during a difficult period in his career, adding: "He has recognised the various unhealthy coping mechanisms ... that led to this offence."
Judge Allman said Sterling "made a deliberate and entirely selfish decision to drive your vehicle without adequate sleep and whilst consuming a Class C drug ... exposing a large number of road users to a significant risk of serious harm".
But, she added, Sterling had substantial personal mitigation, including his charitable work and his engagement with addiction services since the incident.

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is set to reignite global trade tensions with new tariffs on major trading partners, sources said, undeterred in his protectionist push by major losses by his Republican Party in US midterm elections.
The Trump administration's announcement, expected imminently, will address what it has argued is excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday (Nov 24).
They include China, which is poised to rack up a record trade surplus of well over US$1 trillion in 2026, though the tariff level is expected to remain within the range agreed under the current truce between Trump and his counterpart Xi Jinping.
The prospect of new US tariffs was a further factor weighing on global stock markets on Wednesday as a tech-led rally continued to run out of steam, with Nasdaq futures down over 2 per cent.

"It is another reminder that while the legal justification for tariffs keeps changing, US protectionism is becoming increasingly difficult to unwind," ING analysts wrote in a note.
On Wednesday, Beijing reiterated its opposition to "trade wars" and once again dismissed the notion of overcapacity, but stopped short of threatening retaliation.
"The so-called 'overcapacity' is a false issue, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation," foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said.
"Both China and the United States should jointly implement the important consensus reached by their heads of state and maintain the stable development of bilateral economic and trade relations," Guo said.

Related:

China warns US against imposing new tariffs

Courtesy for courtesy, curbs for curbs? The two sides of Trump-Xi reciprocity

TARIFF WALL Analysts say, however, higher US trade barriers against China and other economies are the direction of travel, even if the Democratic Party - which won majorities in both houses of Congress earlier this month - tried to curb Trump's tariff impulses.
The tariffs have in part contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the US, a major source of discontent among voters.
"Without the two-thirds majority needed to override a presidential veto, Democrats' ability to dismantle the tariff wall will remain limited," ING analysts said in a note.
"Either way, we don't think the blue wave will mark a return to free trade. The Biden years already showed that tariffs in strategically important sectors enjoy support across political camps."
The US-China truce runs until Jan 10, but many expect it to be extended - potentially as early as next month when Trump and Xi are set to meet again at a G20 gathering in Miami - given the major impact a re-escalation of tit-for-tat hikes similar to those seen in 2025 would have on both economies.
The agreement caps Trump's second-term tariffs on Chinese goods at 20 per cent, in addition to duties of about 25 per cent imposed during his first term. The US has already imposed a 12.5 per cent anti-forced labour duty on all Chinese imports, leaving only 7.5 per cent to reach the 20 per cent cap.
The US and China are also working to cut tariffs on US$30 billion of non-strategic imports from each side.

Related:

DPM Gan Kim Yong visits US amid 12.5% tariff on Singapore exports

Singapore takes trade compliance seriously, will take firm action against businesses that break laws: MTI

Commentary: Trump’s tariff wall isn’t going anywhere

TAILORED RATES One of the people said that the duties would be specifically tailored to each country, with goods from Mexico and Norway unlikely to see any immediate levies.
The White House is expected to honour capped tariff rates that were included in finalised US trade deals with partner countries, this person said. These include duty ceilings of 15 per cent on goods from the EU, Japan and South Korea and 19 per cent for Malaysia.
The US also is expected to honour the 20 per cent cap on Trump's second-term tariffs on goods from China, as long as a trade truce with Beijing is extended. If it expires, the Chinese excess capacity rate would rise to a higher level.
The USTR and the White House did not respond to Reuters queries about the pending announcement.
REPLACEMENT TARIFFS The trading partners included in the probe are China, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Switzerland, Norway, Singapore, Bangladesh and Cambodia, along with the European Union.
USTR launched the excess capacity probe in March, under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, along with a separate investigation into weak or lax enforcement of anti-forced labour laws in 59 countries and the European Union. Together, the duties are meant to rebuild Trump's global "Liberation Day" tariffs that were struck down by the US Supreme Court in February.
The Trump administration has singled out China as the biggest source of excess industrial capacity, which it says is flooding global markets with steel, aluminium, electric vehicles, appliances, solar products and other goods. China says its exports reflect competitive advantages.

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is set to reignite global trade tensions with new tariffs on major trading partners, sources said, undeterred in his protectionist push by major losses by his Republican Party in US midterm elections.
The Trump administration's announcement, expected imminently, will address what it has argued is excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday (Nov 24).
They include China, which is poised to rack up a record trade surplus of well over US$1 trillion in 2026, though the tariff level is expected to remain within the range agreed under the current truce between Trump and his counterpart Xi Jinping.
The prospect of new US tariffs was a further factor weighing on global stock markets on Wednesday as a tech-led rally continued to run out of steam, with Nasdaq futures down over 2 per cent.

On Wednesday, Beijing reiterated its opposition to "trade wars" and once again dismissed the notion of overcapacity, but stopped short of threatening retaliation.
"The so-called 'overcapacity' is a false issue, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation," foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said.
"Both China and the United States should jointly implement the important consensus reached by their heads of state and maintain the stable development of bilateral economic and trade relations," Guo said.

Related:

TARIFF WALL Analysts say, however, higher US trade barriers against China and other economies are the direction of travel, even if the Democratic Party - which won majorities in both houses of Congress earlier this month - tried to curb Trump's tariff impulses.
The tariffs have in part contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the US, a major source of discontent among voters.
"Without the two-thirds majority needed to override a presidential veto, Democrats' ability to dismantle the tariff wall will remain limited," ING analysts said in a note.
"Either way, we don't think the blue wave will mark a return to free trade. The Biden years already showed that tariffs in strategically important sectors enjoy support across political camps."
The US-China truce runs until Jan 10, but many expect it to be extended - potentially as early as next month when Trump and Xi are set to meet again at a G20 gathering in Miami - given the major impact a re-escalation of tit-for-tat hikes similar to those seen in 2025 would have on both economies.
The agreement caps Trump's second-term tariffs on Chinese goods at 20 per cent, in addition to duties of about 25 per cent imposed during his first term. The US has already imposed a 12.5 per cent anti-forced labour duty on all Chinese imports, leaving only 7.5 per cent to reach the 20 per cent cap.
The US and China are also working to cut tariffs on US$30 billion of non-strategic imports from each side.

The US also is expected to honour the 20 per cent cap on Trump's second-term tariffs on goods from China, as long as a trade truce with Beijing is extended. If it expires, the Chinese excess capacity rate would rise to a higher level.

CoreWeave Debt Rout Sends a Stark Warning Across the AI Industry Less than 1 min read

CRWV
Investor doubts about the financing behind the AI buildout are spilling into corporate credit, putting CoreWeave CRWV debt among the market's weakest performers on Tuesday.
The pressure suggests scrutiny is spreading beyond a single borrower.
All four of CoreWeave's major bond issues fell to their weakest prices since issuance in afternoon trading Tuesday, Bloomberg reported, citing Trace data. Its 9.625% notes due July 2032 dropped as much as 4.6 points to 74.9 cents on the dollar, while the 9.75% notes maturing in October 2031 declined 3.75 points to 76.3 cents.
The company's 9% bonds due February 2031 lost as much as 3.6 points to 76.6 cents, and its 9.25% notes due June 2030 fell three points to 80.9 cents. The declines wiped out a brief advance from Monday.
Stress was also visible in credit protection markets. A basket of credit-default swaps tied to major hyperscalers rose more than 7% to a record-wide 115.6, according to ZeroHedge. These contracts provide protection against debt defaults. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2% Tuesday after gaining 6.5% in the previous session.

items.title: ＥＵ、500億ユーロ規模の株式ファンド計画　量子技術振興へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Foo Yun Chee　Charlotte Van Campenhout

[ブリュッセル ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Foo Yun Chee　Charlotte Van Campenhout

[ブリュッセル ２５日 ロイター] - 欧州連合（ＥＵ）欧州委員会は２５日、２０３０年までに欧州を量子技術の世界的リーダーとするため、５００億ユーロ（５４７億３０００万ドル）規模の株式ファンドの設立に加え、調達入札において欧州企業を優遇するその他措置を提案した。

「量子法案」は、ＡＩ（人工知能）開発、半導体、クラウドコンピューティングの分野で米国や中国に後れを取っている欧州が、第三国への依存度を低減できるよう支援することを目的としている。

また、米国企業が「キルスイッチ」を使用して欧州での自社製品の機能を遮断する可能性があることへの懸念が高まっている中、ＥＵは現地での製品・サービスの開発に注力している。

ビルクネン欧州委員（技術担当）は「量子技術は産業、安全保障、イノベーションの未来を形作り、われわれの社会に多大な影響を与えるだろう。欧州は今、その取り組みを加速させる必要がある」と声明で述べた。

この法案は、法律として成立する前に、今後数カ月の間にＥＵ加盟国および欧州議会との間で調整を行う必要がある。

欧州委によると、世界の量子関連企業の約３分の１がＥＵに拠点を置いている。昨年の量子技術への公的資金は８６億ユーロに達したが、米国は５３億ユーロ、中国は１３６億ユーロだった。

しかし、量子スタートアップに対する欧州の民間資金は１１億ユーロにとどまり、米国の７０億ユーロには及ばなかった。

法案は「量子技術が安全保障やＥＵの戦略的利益、技術的自立に及ぼしうる影響を考慮すると、調達手続きを、ＥＵの管理下にある事業体が提供する製品、システム、サービスに限定する必要がある」と述べている。

また、ＥＵが相互パートナーシップを結んでいる第三国の事業体も、入札に参加できるとしている。

FAST

MUMBAI, Nov 25 : Indian fintech PhonePe has resumed preparations for its initial public offering and is targeting a listing in the first three months of next year at a valuation of $12 billion to $15 billion, a person directly aware of the discussions said.
The Walmart-backed company is expected to file its updated draft papers with India's market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, within the next 30 to 45 days, the person said, requesting anonymity as talks are confidential.
The listing is set to be India's biggest fintech debut since Paytm's $2.5 billion float in 2021. PhonePe had paused its listing plans in March due to global capital market volatility stoked by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
The issue will be an entirely secondary share sale to raise $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion, retaining the size outlined in PhonePe's January draft prospectus, where majority owner Walmart said it would trim its stake by about 12 per cent, and investors Tiger Global and Microsoft planned to fully exit.

PhonePe, the dominant player in digital payments in India with over 650 million registered users, processed nearly 11.4 billion of the country's 25.4 billion Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions in October.
Indian business daily The Economic Times on Wednesday first reported PhonePe's plans to resume its IPO.
Walmart and PhonePe didn't immediately respond to Reuters' email seeking comment.
The Bengaluru-based fintech, which competes with Google Pay and Paytm in India, expects to turn profitable in the next fiscal year, excluding any fee revenue on UPI and government digital payments incentives, according to the person cited above.
India bars banks and fintech platforms like PhonePe from charging fees on standard UPI transfers to encourage digital adoption. A government proposal to introduce a 0.4 per cent merchant fee on transactions exceeding 2,000 rupees ($21) was recently deferred indefinitely following opposition from retailers.

items.summary: [ドバイ ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ドバイ ２５日 ロイター] - イランのイスラム革命防衛隊海軍は国営メディアを通じて声明を出し、２５日にホルムズ海峡で２隻の石油タンカーが機雷に接触し、爆発・炎上したと発表した。

２隻は無許可の航路で海峡を通過しようとしていたという。

これとは別に、イラン陸軍は、同海峡の監視と統制を強化するため、軍が新たなシステムを導入し、既存のシステムをアップグレードしたと表明。報道官は、イラン軍と調整せずに海峡を通過する船舶はより大きなリスクに直面しており、ここ数週間で機雷に接触する事例が発生していると警告した。

items.title: イスラエル軍がアパート空爆、ハマス治安幹部と家族殺害　連日の攻撃
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Nidal al-Mughrabi

[カイロ ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Nidal al-Mughrabi

[カイロ ２５日 ロイター] - イスラエル軍は２５日未明、パレスチナ自治区ガザのアパートを空爆し、イスラム組織ハマスの治安幹部を妻、子ども２人と共に殺害した。ハマスが運営するガザ内務省と医療関係者が明らかにした。

死亡したのはハマスの内部治安機関幹部モハメド・アブエルーフ氏と家族。医療関係者によると、空爆はガザ市西部の海岸近くにあるビーチ難民キャンプ内のアブエルーフ氏のアパートを直撃した。

同日午前にはガザ市北部のカラマ地区でもイスラエル軍による別の空爆があり、１人が死亡したという。

イスラエル軍はコメントの求めに対し、ガザで「複数の軍事工作員を標的にした」と説明した。詳細は追って発表するとしている。

２４日にはハマス内部治安機関トップ、ナイーム・アブナヘル氏がイスラエル軍に殺害されている。

FAST

BRUSSELS, Nov 25 : A European Union meeting expected to consider Tesla's bid to win approval for its assisted self-driving system across the bloc has been postponed for Dec. 15, a European Commission spokesperson told Reuters on Wednesday.
The Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles (TCMV) had been expected to potentially vote on the system during its December meeting, after no vote was held at two earlier meetings following preliminary approval from the Netherlands in April.
The vote is a key hurdle in Tesla's push to bring the technology to Europe. Nearly a dozen countries have followed the Dutch lead, with Italy the most populous to begin a rollout, but EU-wide approval requires support from at least 15 of the bloc's 27 countries representing 65 per cent of its population.
The meeting was originally scheduled for Dec. 1, Dutch regulator RDW told Reuters. Belgium's Flanders transport ministry initially said it had been moved to Dec. 7, before the Commission clarified that it would instead take place on Dec. 15.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Oil money helped N.L.'s debt, but experts say the province still needs a plan
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: An oil windfall has helped the Newfoundland and Labrador government reduce its sizable debt, but some experts say the province still needs a long-term plan to pay off the balance.
items.body: ST. JOHN’S — An oil windfall has helped the Newfoundland and Labrador government reduce its sizable debt, but some experts say the province still needs a long-term plan to pay off the balance. A comparison of budgets and financial updates across Canada shows Newfoundland and Labrador’s per-capita net debt is expected to be the highest among the provinces for the current fiscal year, which ends in March. Economist Wade Locke said the provincial government would have to have a budget surplus of roughly $350 million a year for the next three decades to bring its per-capita net debt down to the Canadian average. That’s assuming a constant interest rate of about 3.6 per cent, he said in an interview Tuesday. “The problem is so massive. It’s going to require a huge effort and a well laid-out plan,” said Locke, a retired professor at Memorial University. “It’s not just a matter of picking numbers off a spreadsheet.” That plan should include changes to legislation requiring subsequent governments to follow through with it, particularly since reigning in spending and reducing debt are not popular policies, he added. Newfoundland and Labrador’s Progressive Conservative government delivered an economic update on Monday projecting a surplus of $78 million at the end of the 2026-27 fiscal year and a reduced net debt. It was a sharp contrast to the budget tabled in April which forecast a $688 million deficit. The province’s net debt is now expected to reach $19.3 billion by the end of March, rather than the $20.8 billion laid out in the budget. About $1.2 billion — or just under 10 per cent of the province’s entire budget — will have to pay for debt servicing costs, including interest. Government officials said the new numbers were driven by nearly $1.5 billion in extra revenue, most of which comes from the soaring oil prices that followed military strikes against Iran by the U.S. and Israel earlier this year. Newfoundland and Labrador is home to four offshore oil installations, and production is up at all of them, Craig Pardy, the province’s finance minister, told reporters in St. John’s on Monday. Pardy had previously promised to deliver a debt management plan with his fall fiscal update. On Monday, he announced a $175-million investment into a new sinking fund, which officials said would mature to $750 million by 2052 and be used to pay off debt. Locke noted the sinking fund money would only cover about four per cent of what the province currently owes. Pardy said Monday that the province’s gross domestic product is expected to grow this fiscal year by 7.1 per cent, a number that leads the country. He also pointed to possible returns from Equinor’s proposed Bay du Nord offshore oil project and a new energy agreement with Quebec, neither of which have been finalized. But Renaud Brossard said the anticipated economic activity may not be enough to counter some of the headwinds facing the province. One in four people in Newfoundland and Labrador are 65 or older, and seniors tend to pay fewer taxes and need more health care, said Brossard, who is the vice president of communications for the Montreal Economic Institute think tank “There absolutely needs to be a debt management plan,” Brossard said in an interview. In a news release Tuesday, the Canadian Taxpayers Federation applauded the Newfoundland and Labrador government’s move to squirrel away much of its oil windfall rather than spend it. Both Locke and Brossard had similar praise. However, in an email, Devin Drover, the federation’s Atlantic director, acknowledged Pardy’s fiscal update on Monday delivered debt reduction, but not a “debt management plan per se.” “Taxpayers still owe … over $19 billion, and that bill comes due whether oil prices co-operate or not,” Drover said. He suggested the province introduce legislation requiring that windfall money be used to pay off debt. He also said the province needs to make clear debt-reduction targets and reign in spending. “If the government locks that in, this year’s progress becomes a turning point instead of a one-off,” Drover said. The previous Liberal government introduced a “future fund” with mandatory annual contributions to help pay off debt. The Progressive Conservatives axed the annual requirement rules earlier this year, saying it didn’t make sense to borrow more for the fund. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 24, 2026.

Bayern said they held talks with the player's management team on Tuesday amid speculation about his contract situation following comments by senior club officials over Musiala's future and whether he could ever perform again at the highest level.
The comments from honorary president Uli Hoeness and board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, among others, were strongly criticised by the German players' union.

LONDON, Nov 25 : Online fast-fashion retailer Shein warned on Wednesday that its European business may not recover until the second half of next year after new e-commerce import fees hit sales in its biggest market and dragged down group revenue.
Shein's third-quarter results are the first to show the impact of the European Union's €3 ($3.28) fee on e-commerce imports, which has eroded its competitive edge just as the newly listed company seeks to bolster confidence in its business model.
Quarterly revenue in Europe fell 27.6 per cent to $2.98 billion after Shein raised prices to offset the additional costs. Group revenue fell 6 per cent to $10.27 billion.
CEO Sky Xu said sales in Europe might not recover until the second half of 2027, when most deliveries would be made from European warehouses the company is investing in.

"We expect the EU to remain under pressure for the next few quarters," Xu said on a call with analysts.
Shein's business model has come under further pressure since the start of November, when the EU began imposing an additional €2 fee on e-commerce parcels.
MARKETING SPEND SLASHED
Facing a sharp slowdown in sales, Shein cut marketing spending by 41.5 per cent in the quarter, reducing online advertising to protect profitability. Operating income rose 17 per cent from a year earlier to $743 million.
Once one of the fastest-growing online retailers, Shein helped intensify price competition for established rivals such as H&M and Zara. But its rapid expansion has stalled since the US and Europe removed duty-free access for e-commerce imports.
"Consumers worldwide have become more cautious," the company said in a statement, adding that shoppers are placing more emphasis on value for money.

FAST

Nov 25 : Former South Africa captain AB de Villiers said lessons must be learnt from the 2018 ball-tampering scandal involving Australia but urged the sport to move on from "Sandpapergate".
The debate was reignited this year after Australia batter Usman Khawaja alleged in his book that knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball in the test series in South Africa extended beyond the three players who were punished, Cameron Bancroft, David Warner and Steve Smith.
"Let's not blow it out of proportion. Let's move on now. But also we need to take learning from that," De Villiers told reporters during a virtual roundtable organised by Test Twenty20, a new format of cricket played across genders using both red and white balls. 
"A mistake was made. We can't hide from that fact. And I think it affects the whole cricketing world, not just Australia," De Villiers said.

"We all want the game to be in a good position, right? But let's remember these things have happened in the past as well, and we found a way to move on.
"So let's now move on, and the youngsters take responsibility to bring great energy and great integrity into the game of cricket."
Australia won the opening test in Durban before South Africa claimed the next three matches to seal a 3-1 series victory.
REVERSE SWING UNDER THREAT
De Villiers scored an unbeaten century to guide South Africa to victory in the second test in Port Elizabeth and was at the crease when Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball during the third game in Cape Town.
"As long as the players don't step over the line, we all know where that line is," De Villiers said.
"Sometimes it's a little bit grey, and that's where the administrators come in. They need to clear it up completely and find a way for reverse swing to survive and still be around for many years to come.
"I feel it's part and parcel of the game, and it's great for the bowlers to have that. It really speeds the game up."

FAST

LONDON, Nov 25 : Retailers heading into the Black Friday shopping period face growing cyber threats as artificial intelligence makes attacks faster and more potent, at a time when the sector has some of the lowest levels of cyber insurance protection.
The post-Thanksgiving spree has long represented a lucrative sales opportunity, but more frequent and sophisticated cyberattacks are increasingly testing retailers' cyber resilience.
Ransomware attacks on retail, leisure and hospitality businesses are 50 per cent more frequent in November than the monthly average, according to claims data from insurer CFC. Only 43 per cent of small and medium-sized retailers carry cyber insurance, compared with 81 per cent in financial services and 71 per cent in technology.
"Retailers spend months making sure their websites, stock and logistics can withstand the surge in customers. But Black Friday should be treated as a resilience exercise as much as a revenue opportunity," said Lindsey Maher, CFC's head of global cyber development.

Black Friday and Cyber Monday bookend one of the retail sector's busiest periods of the year, with consumers searching for deals and retailers often offering hefty discounts.
UK shoppers looking to snap up bargains are set to spend £235 ($307) each this Black Friday, with UK spending expected to reach its highest since 2022, research from PwC shows.
Retailers don't generally buy additional cyber insurance for a weekend and focus instead on testing and strengthening resilience, said David Molony, Europe, Middle East and Africa head of cyber and financial sponsors at Aon. That matters most at a time of year when revenue depends heavily on technology, he said.
"A cyber incident that interrupts the ability to trade during peak season can move very quickly from an operational issue to a material financial loss," he said.
US retailer Target incurred net cumulative expenses of $202 million after a 2013 breach during the holiday shopping season that compromised at least 40 million credit cards, the company has said.
Complex retail supply chains, copious credit card records and the busy shopping period mean retailers are primed for maximum chaos and interruption, said Sydonie Williams, head of international cyber risks at Beazley. While AI increases the threat risk, it also improves defence mechanisms, she said.
Francisco Donoso, chief product and technology officer at Beazley Security, said AI was speeding up attacks and the number of vulnerabilities being exposed was almost six times higher than a year ago.
"It's really hard for organisations to keep up," Donoso said.
($1 = 0.7639 pounds)

Source: Reuters

items.title: India-UK investment treaty talks stall amid differences, pact unlikely soon
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: A bilateral investment treaty protects companies' investments in each other's countries and provides a way to resolve disputes with governments ...
items.body: India does not plan to aggressively pursue a bilateral investment treaty with Britain in the near term, as differences over taxation and access to international arbitration continue to stall negotiations, two senior government officials said.India's reluctance comes as it seeks to negotiate investment treaties alongside trade agreements with major partners, including the European Union and Canada, to provide reciprocal protection to investors and boost confidence in cross-border investments.A bilateral investment treaty protects companies' investments in each other's countries and provides a way to resolve disputes with governments.British companies, including Vodafone and Cairn, have won international arbitration cases against India over retrospective tax claims and the cancellation of contracts worth billions of dollars.About a decade ago, India allowed treaties with over 50 countries to lapse and then designed a law that limits the protection offered to investors. That law is also under review.The first source, who is involved in the discussions and not authorised to speak to the media, said the talks had lost momentum and a pact was unlikely in the near term.New Delhi wants to preserve its sovereign right to set tax and regulatory policy, while Britain wants stronger investor protections, including easier access to international arbitration, the source said.The differences kept the treaty from being concluded alongside the countries' free trade agreement, which took effect on July 15, they said.Emails sent to India's trade and finance ministries seeking comment did not receive a response. The UK's finance ministry also did not respond to a request for comment.The UK was India's ninth-largest source of foreign direct investment equity inflows in 2025/26, investing more than $1 billion, according to government data.Officials from both countries are expected to meet in early December for the UK-India Economic and Financial Dialogue, a ministerial-level forum covering macroeconomic policy, financial regulation, taxation and climate finance, the second source said. However, the investment treaty will not be discussed there, they added.The dialogue, co-chaired by India's finance minister and Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, will be the first under UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government. The two sides last held it in April 2025, under the previous British government.Separately, tensions have risen recently over India's decision to impose a 162.5% import duty on bulk Scotch whisky, which has prompted a dispute with liquor firms including Pernod Ricard and Diageo.INDIA REVIEWS INVESTMENT TREATY FRAMEWORKIndia's stance reflects a broader effort to limit the exposure of domestic policy decisions to international legal challenges following high-profile arbitration disputes.In 2015, New Delhi proposed a new treaty framework that excludes tax and prevents investors from seeking international arbitration before exhausting local remedies. It has since signed revised agreements with countries including the United Arab Emirates, Uzbekistan, Israel, Belarus and Kyrgyzstan.The 2015 model is now being reviewed again. India plans to retain the requirement that foreign investors exhaust local legal remedies before seeking international arbitration, though the mandatory five-year period could be shortened to two years, the second source said.Treaties signed with the UAE in 2024 and Israel in 2025, both now in force, allow investors to seek international arbitration after three years instead of five.The government is close to securing Cabinet approval for a revised model treaty that will serve as the basis for negotiations with individual countries, a senior official told reporters in September.India is currently negotiating free trade agreements with at least eight countries, alongside parallel investment treaty talks with many of them.

Nov 25 : The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) will appeal the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling to reinstate Russia in next year's world championship to the Swiss Federal Tribunal, the governing body said on Wednesday.
Russia had been banned from IIHF competitions since 2022 following the nation's invasion of Ukraine.
On October 30, CAS upheld appeals lodged by the Russian Ice Hockey Federation over its exclusion from IIHF competitions for the 2026-27 season, saying the IIHF had not provided sufficient evidence to justify its assessment that security concerns required Russia's continued exclusion.
Media reported that the IIHF had filed a challenge with CAS based on the non-disclosure of ties to Russia by two of the three CAS panel members involved in the decision.

"The decision is based on concerns around the independence and impartiality of two of the three arbitrators on the CAS Panel," the IIHF statement said.
"Especially following the information that has recently come to light regarding potential links between the two arbitrators and Russia.
"Given the significance of the ruling and its implications for international ice hockey, the IIHF considers it definitively essential to pursue the matter before the Swiss Federal Tribunal.
Although CAS awards are considered final, sporting bodies can appeal to the Swiss Federal Tribunal on valid legal grounds.
RULING FALLOUT
CAS has acknowledged the divisive reaction to its ruling, but reiterated that the decision was based solely on the evidence submitted.
Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Latvia, Norway and Sweden have said they would refuse to face Russia. One sponsor, AJ Products, has withdrawn, while others have said they could do so if Russia takes part.
Russia will not compete in next month's 2027 World Junior Championship after Canada said it would deny entry to Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials coming to compete, even those with valid visas.
The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the IIHF's decision to keep the tournament in Canada "unacceptable and unlawful".
Russian athletes will also not be allowed into the Czech Republic, which is hosting the women's Under-18 ice hockey world championship in January.

items.title: コロンビアのスーパー立てこもり、人質全員救出　中部では爆弾事件
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Nelson Bocanegra　Julia Symmes Cobb

[ボゴタ ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Nelson Bocanegra　Julia Symmes Cobb

[ボゴタ ２５日 ロイター] - コロンビアの都市カルタヘナのスーパーマーケットで武装した男らが人質をとっていた事件で、２５日未明に治安部隊が作戦を実施し全員を救出、１日におよぶ立てこもりが終結した。

デラエスプリエジャ大統領は、午前１時３０分（０６３０ＧＭＴ、日本時間午後３時３０分）に発信した動画で、人質全員を救出したとし、犯人の１人が死亡したと発表した。

身元不明の犯人グループは、商業施設から現金を輸送していた装甲車の乗っ取りに失敗。その後スーパーで約３０人を人質に取り立てこもった。２４日には１０人が解放されていた。

中部の都市ビジャビセンシオでは２３日夜、政府庁舎付近で自動車爆弾が爆発し、２２人が負傷した。犯行声明は出ていないが、政府は２０１６年の和平合意を拒否する旧左翼ゲリラ、コロンビア革命軍（ＦＡＲＣ）の反主流派組織による犯行と非難した。デラエスプリエジャ大統領はビジャビセンシオを訪問後、カルタヘナに向かっていた。

コロンビアでは６０年以上にわたり、コカイン取引を資金源とする内戦が続き、左翼武装組織が政府や、犯罪組織化した右翼民兵組織と戦ってきた。政府とＦＡＲＣが１６年に結んだ和平合意は一定の戦闘沈静化につながり、今週で締結から１０年を迎えた。しかし、犯罪組織は依然として強大な勢力を維持し、小規模な反政府武装組織も存続している。

items.title: China y Estados Unidos abrirán un nuevo capítulo en las negociaciones comerciales, dice exnegociador
items.author: Josh Xiao, Avril Hong
items.summary: El exviceministro de Hacienda de China Zhu Guangyao anticipa una nueva etapa de diálogo entre Pekín y Washington cuando retomen las negociaciones en enero, antes del vencimiento de la tregua arancelar ...
items.body: Bloomberg — China y Estados Unidos lograrán mayores avances una vez que se reanuden las negociaciones comerciales en enero, cuando está previsto que expire la tregua arancelaria que dura ya un año, según un antiguo negociador de alto rango de Pekín. “Abrirán un nuevo capítulo y lograrán que las relaciones comerciales entre China y EE.UU. sean más saludables”, afirmó Zhu Guangyao, que fue viceministro de Hacienda de China entre 2010 y 2018, en una entrevista concedida el miércoles a Bloomberg TV en Singapur. Aunque puedan persistir “algunas diferencias”, Zhu señaló que los negociadores “seguirán dialogando y avanzando paso a paso”. Ver más: China extiende la tregua de minerales críticos con EE.UU. en medio de nuevas restricciones a chips Sus comentarios optimistas se producen pocos días después de la visita del presidente Donald Trump a Shenzhen para mantener conversaciones con el líder chino Xi Jinping durante una reunión de las economías de Asia-Pacífico. Tanto Xi como Trump parecieron apoyarse en gran medida en su buena relación personal para mantener estables las relaciones entre sus países, a pesar de que han surgido nuevas tensiones entre las mayores economías del mundo, incluido un supuesto escándalo de espionaje en el que está implicado el director ejecutivo de Nvidia Corp.( NVDA ), Jensen Huang. Zhu, quien desempeñó un papel clave en las negociaciones comerciales entre EE.UU. y China durante el primer mandato de Trump, espera una mejor comunicación durante la próxima ronda de conversaciones, ya que ambas partes se benefician del tono marcado por los presidentes. En consecuencia, prevé más avances en el diálogo bilateral sobre inteligencia artificial, incluyendo cuestiones como las pruebas de grandes modelos de lenguaje y las notificaciones mutuas de cualquier emergencia. Hasta su jubilación en 2018, Zhu ocupó el cargo de viceministro de Finanzas y supervisó el Departamento de Aranceles Aduaneros. Más recientemente, fue consejero del Consejo de Estado, el gabinete chino. La actual tregua comercial, alcanzada el año pasado en Corea del Sur, se extiende hasta enero e incluye una reducción de los aranceles, junto con una suspensión de los controles adicionales de China sobre las exportaciones de tierras raras, que están previstos que expiren el 10 de enero. Los negociadores comerciales de EE.UU. y China se han reunido en ocho ocasiones desde que Trump regresó a la Casa Blanca a principios del año pasado. China ha tomado recientemente medidas para evitar desestabilizar la tregua. El martes, Pekín prorrogó la suspensión de las restricciones de exportación estadounidenses para algunos minerales críticos. Ver más: Trump prepara nuevos aranceles a productos de China, la UE y más de una docena de economías Ya este mismo martes, Estados Unidos tiene previsto anunciar planes para aumentar los aranceles sobre productos procedentes de países como China, en un momento en que la administración Trump se dispone a sustituir los gravámenes anulados por el Tribunal Supremo. Se prevé que estos aranceles se dirijan contra aquellas economías acusadas de perjudicar a la industria estadounidense mediante la concesión de subvenciones a sus fabricantes nacionales, según ha informado Bloomberg News. Se espera que los aranceles sobre los productos chinos tengan un alcance más amplio que los aplicados a los artículos de otros países y que carezcan de exenciones, aunque se mantendrán dentro de los límites de la tregua comercial. Zhu afirmó que las cuestiones derivadas de la investigación de Washington sobre el exceso de capacidad de producción, en virtud del artículo 301 de la Ley de Comercio de 1974, pueden resolverse mediante negociaciones. El crecimiento económico de China superará el 4,5% en 2027, señaló, y añadió que es posible que se aplique una política fiscal expansionista durante el próximo año. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de China calificó el miércoles la perspectiva de nuevos aranceles estadounidenses sobre sus exportaciones de “maniobra política” y afirmó que ambos países deberían colaborar para mantener su tregua comercial. items.title: Bonos japoneses a 40 años registran menor demanda en medio de la aversión global al riesgo
items.author: John Cheng
items.summary: La relación entre oferta y demanda cayó a 2,63, por debajo de la subasta anterior y de la media de los últimos 12 meses. La incertidumbre global y la volatilidad de los mercados redujeron el interés p ...
items.body: Bloomberg — La subasta de bonos del Estado japonés a 40 años celebrada este miércoles registró una menor demanda, ya que el clima de aversión al riesgo a nivel mundial lastró el interés de los inversores. La relación entre la oferta y la demanda se situó en 2,63, frente al 3,10 de la última subasta y a una media de los últimos 12 meses de 2,75. El rendimiento de los bonos fue del 4,09%, frente al 4,125% de la subasta anterior. Ver más: Acciones asiáticas caen ante renovadas dudas sobre el auge de la inteligencia artificial Los rendimientos de los bonos del Estado japonés han subido en las últimas semanas en medio de una ola de ventas de bonos del Tesoro estadounidense, ya que los inversores descuentan una mayor probabilidad de que la Reserva Federal aplique nuevas medidas de endurecimiento monetario para contener la inflación. El nerviosismo en torno a las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial también ha contribuido a una mayor volatilidad general del mercado. Este débil resultado “refleja un sentimiento global de aversión al riesgo impulsado por la elevada incertidumbre en torno a las acciones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, así como la continua liquidación de posiciones de aplanamiento tras el retroceso de las expectativas de subidas de tipos por parte del Banco de Japón”, afirmó Ryutaro Kimura, estratega senior de renta fija de BNP Paribas Asset Management. Los inversores parecen preferir los bonos con duraciones más cortas frente a los bonos del Estado japonés (JGB) de plazo muy largo, añadió. Se trata de una subasta de bonos del Estado japonés (JGB) a 40 años decepcionante, lo que sugiere que el apetito por el riesgo en Japón es limitado a medida que el año llega a su fin. La demanda se situó por debajo de la media anual y el rendimiento máximo se situó ligeramente por encima de las previsiones previas a la venta. Estos datos apuntan a un potencial alcista limitado para los bonos en el mercado secundario. — Mark Cranfield, estratega de Markets Live. Una venta de bonos a 40 años celebrada en septiembre registró su mayor demanda en seis años, pero los rendimientos han caído ligeramente desde entonces. El rendimiento a 40 años se situó por última vez en el 4,145%, frente al máximo histórico del 4,355% alcanzado en mayo. A diferencia de las ventas convencionales de bonos del Estado japonés (JGB), el plazo de 40 años utiliza un formato de subasta holandesa, en el que todos los adjudicatarios pagan el precio mínimo aceptado, lo que reduce el riesgo de pagar de más y podría fomentar la demanda. Este plazo suele estar dominado por las aseguradoras de vida que buscan equilibrar sus pasivos a largo plazo. Ver más: Alibaba evalúa emitir bonos en el exterior en 2027 para financiar su expansión en IA El presupuesto fiscal de Japón para el año 2027 sigue siendo una fuente de incertidumbre para el mercado de bonos. Los inversores están atentos a cómo el Gobierno de la primera ministra Sanae Takaichi tiene previsto financiar el aumento del gasto en defensa y la reducción del impuesto sobre el consumo, y a si ello requerirá una mayor emisión de bonos. items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Munsif Vengattil　Aditya Kalra　Saurabh Sharma

[ニューデリー ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Munsif Vengattil　Aditya Kalra　Saurabh Sharma

[ニューデリー ２５日 ロイター] -  米メタのインド部門幹部が、同国の野党・国民会議派と非公開で会談した。関係者４人が明らかにした。メタのコンテンツ管理手法に対する抗議活動の沈静化を目指す。

関係者１人によると、会合は２４日に国民会議派の本部で開かれた。別の関係者３人によると、メタ側は自社のオフィスを標的にした抗議活動や、与党の母体であるヒンズー至上主義団体の制服を着たマーク・ザッカーバーグ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）を描いたポスターについて懸念を伝えた。

一方、国民会議派側は、党幹部のアカウントや投稿に対する制限が増えていることや、モディ首相率いる与党・インド人民党（ＢＪＰ）をメタが優遇しているとの疑惑に懸念を示したという。

２０日に同党の青年組織による抗議活動が始まって以来、メタが同党と直接対話するのは初めて。

国民会議派の青年組織「インド青年会議」は、政府の命令で削除されたアカウントの復旧や、アルゴリズムが投稿を制限する仕組みの説明を要求している。メンバーらはハイデラバード、ムンバイ、グルグラムにあるメタのオフィス周辺で警察と衝突した。

協議の内容を直接知る関係者によると、メタ側は会合で同党に何も約束はせず、現地の法律に縛られていると説明した。また、全ての政党に対して中立であると強調したという。

メタの開示資料によると、現地の法律に基づき２０２６年上半期に制限した投稿やアカウントは５４０万件を超え、２５年通年の約７万件から急増した。インドの情報技術（ＩＴ）規則が改正され、より迅速で積極的な削除が義務付けられたためとしている。

items.title: 豪、ネット企業に有害コンテンツ削除義務　法案可決・1年後施行
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [シドニー ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[シドニー ２５日 ロイター] - オーストラリアは、インターネット企業に対し、有害なコンテンツや機能を積極的に排除することを義務付け、これに従わない場合は世界全体の売上高の最大５％の罰金を科す法案を可決した。ビッグテック規制の柱となるもので、表現の自由を擁護する団体からは非難を浴びている。

「デジタル・デューティー・オブ・ケア」は１年後に施行され、これまでバラバラだったオンライン行動規範に代わり、包括的な法律として導入される。政府はこの法律により、プラットフォーム事業者にオーストラリア国民の安全を最優先にする責任が課せられるとしている。

ウェルズ通信相は法案可決後の声明で「『デジタル・デューティー・オブ・ケア』は、シートベルトの着用義務、タバコの無地パッケージ化、銃規制改革に並ぶ、画期的な安全改革だ」と説明。「ビッグテック企業はもはや幻想を抱いてはならない。彼らは自社のプラットフォーム上でオーストラリア国民の安全を守る責任があり、それを果たせなければ責任を問う」と述べた。

同法は、「女性やジェンダー平等に対する敵対的な態度を助長または促進する」コンテンツや、「犯罪を美化したり、危険な行為や深刻な危害を及ぼす行為を助長したりする」コンテンツを禁止しているが、一部の表現の自由擁護派は、こうした分類が広範に解釈される恐れがあると警告していた。

インターネット企業を代表する業界団体ＤＩＧＩは「この法律は依然としてあいまいで、企業がどのように順守すべきか、あるいは新しい規則がどのようにしてオーストラリア人の安全を高めるのかが不明確なままだ」と述べた。

items.title: ETF de bitcoin en EE.UU. se encaminan a su peor mes con salidas cercanas a US$5.000 millones
items.author: Sidhartha Shukla
items.summary: Los fondos acumulan reembolsos netos por US$4.940 millones en noviembre, mientras el bitcoin cae cerca de un 23% y se encamina a su peor desempeño mensual desde junio de 2022.
items.body: Bloomberg — Los fondos cotizados en bolsa (ETF) que invierten en bitcoin y cotizan en EE.UU. se encaminan hacia el peor mes en cuanto a salidas de capital desde su debut en 2024, ya que la persistente ola de ventas de la mayor criptomoneda del mundo está ahuyentando a los inversores. Hasta la fecha, en noviembre se han retirado US$4.940 millones netos de los fondos, según datos recopilados por Bloomberg hasta el 24 de noviembre. El iShares Bitcoin Trust de BlackRock Inc. ( BLK ), el mayor fondo que posee esta criptomoneda, ha sufrido reembolsos por valor de más de US$4.000 millones este mes, lo que también lo sitúa en camino de registrar su peor salida mensual. Ver más: Quién controla realmente las criptomonedas: el poder de Tether y Circle tras el hackeo a Binance Este éxodo se produce mientras el bitcoin cae por debajo de los US$60.000 dólares y se encamina hacia su peor rendimiento mensual desde junio de 2022, cuando una serie de quiebras empresariales desencadenó un colapso generalizado del mercado de las criptomonedas. La criptomoneda ha caído alrededor de un 23% este mes y cotizaba en torno a los US$59.000 a las 14:00 horas del miércoles en Singapur, con un descenso de aproximadamente un 1,3% durante la sesión asiática. Estas pérdidas ponen de manifiesto un brusco cambio de tendencia para un grupo de ETF que contribuyeron a impulsar al alza el bitcoin tras su debut en EE.UU. en enero de 2024. Estos fondos abrieron el acceso a la criptomoneda a un grupo más amplio de inversores institucionales y particulares, y se convirtieron en una importante fuente de demanda durante el mercado alcista. Sus reembolsos récord están reforzando ahora la actual caída, a medida que esa fuente de compra se agota. El bitcoin se recuperó brevemente junto con otros activos de riesgo el lunes, después de que Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) reincorporara a Jensen Huang como CEO, pero desde entonces ha cedido todas esas ganancias, una señal de que los inversores están aprovechando los repuntes para reducir su exposición. “Cuando un mercado no puede mantener un repunte ante buenas noticias, suele significar que los inversores están aprovechando cualquier repunte para vender”, señaló la empresa de análisis de datos Glassnode en una nota. “El bitcoin se negocia las 24 horas del día y tiende a ser uno de los primeros activos en venderse cuando los inversores desean reducir el riesgo”. Ver más: El bitcoin no logra sostener el impulso de Nvidia ante obstáculos para las criptomonedas El bitcoin se enfrenta en estos momentos a numerosos obstáculos, desde ataques informáticos de gran repercusión que han minado la confianza en su seguridad hasta la perspectiva de tasas de interés más altas y un mayor escrutinio regulatorio tras las recientes elecciones de mitad de mandato en EE.UU. La ausencia de demanda estadounidense se suma a la presión, según Glassnode. “Los ETF y otras instituciones constituían una importante fuente de demanda durante la fase alcista, y a estos precios muestran escaso interés”, señaló la empresa. “El retorno de las entradas en los ETF, junto con la compra neta en Coinbase, sería la primera señal de que esto está cambiando”. El bitcoin también se enfrenta a una mayor competencia por el capital de los inversores, ya que el dinero se inclina hacia la renta variable y los activos que ofrecen ingresos, según Ayesha Kiani, directora de operaciones de Monarq Asset Management. El bitcoin está “compitiendo por el mismo capital de riesgo que se está destinando a la renta variable en estos momentos”, declaró Kiani a Bloomberg Television, calificando el éxodo de los ETF como “preocupante”. El sector de las criptomonedas podría necesitar un nuevo catalizador para reactivar la demanda, ahora que las fuerzas que impulsaron el anterior repunte se han desvanecido, afirmó. “Creo que necesitamos encontrar una nueva narrativa, un nuevo catalizador, un nuevo mercado, algo nuevo para todo el sector que nos permita volver a convertirnos en esa clase de activos emergente”, afirmó Kiani. “En este momento existen activos que ofrecen una mayor rentabilidad. Así pues, ¿por qué el bitcoin?" Lea más en Bloomberg.com

FAST

LONDON, Nov 25 : Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East.
Brent crude futures declined 44 cents, or 0.5 per cent, to $90.96 a barrel at 1035 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 62 cents, or 0.8 per cent, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2 per cent on Tuesday.
"Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand," said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage.
On Wednesday, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh's financial district. Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, is part of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast that also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude.

A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to the softer oil prices, Varga said.
US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.
Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average.
"Uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies in the upcoming November 29 meeting, especially with the UAE no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies and Iraq seeking higher oil output capacity, as well as broader market risk-off are some reasons," said Zhenqiang Seto, a senior research specialist for oil at LSEG.
OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy.
"Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno said.
Iraq is pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening tensions over a review that will help determine how much members can pump next year.
Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has also reopened after an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya.
"However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges of attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," Ueno said.
A container ship was targeted and came to a stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media.
On Monday, three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles as they sailed east through the strait, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday.

Source: Reuters

items.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝大幅安、ハイテク株が下げ主導
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [上海 ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[上海 ２５日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落して引けた。上海の主要株価指数は、他市場の動きに押され、３カ月ぶりの大幅安となった。

上海総合指数は２％下落し、２０２５年７月以来の安値で終了。ＣＳＩ３００指数は１．７％下落し、１７カ月以上ぶりの安値で引けた。

ハイテク株が下落を主導。深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は４．２％急落し、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け株式市場「科創板」の科創板５０指数は５．１％急落した。

半導体株は約８％下落した。

野村の中国担当チーフエコノミスト、ティン・ルー氏は「株式市場の調整と、中国による先端ＡＩ半導体や計算資源へのアクセスに対する米政府の規制強化を踏まえると、中国経済は消費の伸び鈍化と固定資産投資の落ち込み拡大により、短期的に一段と強い逆風に直面すると予想する」と述べた。

香港のハンセン指数は１．１％下落し、ハイテク株は２．６％下落した。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Dominique Vidalon　Emma Rumney

[パリ／ロンドン ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Dominique Vidalon　Emma Rumney

[パリ／ロンドン ２５日 ロイター] - 仏酒造大手レミー・コアントローのフランク・マリリー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２５日、２０２９─３０年度までに売上高の伸び率を１桁台後半とする新たな目標を発表した。今年度の利益見通しも引き上げた。

３１─３２年度までの利益率とキャッシュ創出に関する新たな目標も掲げた。

売上高の伸び率は２９─３０年度までに１桁台半ばから後半に達し、それまでの年度は１桁台半ばになる見込み。利益率は少なくとも３００ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）改善し、フリーキャッシュフローの転換率も高める見通しだという。

今年度上半期の営業利益が市場予想を上回る７．８％増となったことを受け、通期の経常営業利益率の見通しを従来の「小幅な」伸びから「堅調な」伸びに引き上げた。

レミー・コアントローは以前、２９─３０年度までに１桁台後半の年間増収率と３３％の営業利益率を目標としていた。

売上高の成長目標は従来とほぼ同じ水準だが、バークレイズのアナリストのローレンス・ワイアット氏は、新たな営業利益率目標の２２％は従来目標に届かないと指摘した。上期の利益が予想を上回ったのは「主にマーケティング・広報費の一時的な削減によるものだ」と分析した。

DUBAI, Nov 25 : Saudi Aramco and its South Korean unit S-Oil on Wednesday inaugurated the $7 billion Shaheen petrochemical project, Aramco's largest investment in South Korea, the Saudi state oil giant said.
• The project in Ulsan is expected to add about 3.2 million metric tons a year of petrochemical production capacity for S-Oil, with commercial operations scheduled to start in 2027 after commissioning, Aramco said in a statement
• "Economic headwinds and rising geopolitical risks do not alter our long-term view on strategic investments," Aramco CEO Amin Nasser was quoted as saying
• He said the project would help meet rising demand for materials used in Asian industries such as electric vehicles and semiconductors

• Shaheen is the first major commercial deployment of Aramco's thermal crude-to-chemicals (TC2C) technology, which it developed with Lummus Technology, Aramco said. The technology is designed to convert a larger share of each barrel of crude directly into chemicals
• The complex includes what Aramco described as the world's largest single steam cracker, along with a propylene fractionator and polymer production units
• The expansion is expected to raise the share of petrochemicals in S-Oil's business portfolio to 25 per cent from 12 per cent, Aramco said
• The facility will be integrated with S-Oil's existing refining and petrochemical operations in Ulsan. It will supply feedstock by pipeline to nearby downstream companies, which will reduce their need for imports
• Aramco holds more than 63 per cent of S-Oil through its subsidiary Aramco Downstream Asia.
